SAVES-1.verified_evidence: src/hooks/useTripClock.ts 38-58: tick() runs on every visibilitychange to visible and every 30 s, calling actions.checkNewDay() and arriveTrip() on the in-memory state. TaskContext.tsx 2424-2430: checkNewDay runs applyDayTransition(prev), which sets lastDate: today() (TaskContext ~1653). That state change triggers the autosave effect (TaskContext 1460-1505), and 1.5 s later it calls cloudSaveByToken(token, {...localRaw, ...state}). On the stale device localRaw is that device's own old copy, so nothing newer gets merged in. The new FC-01 guard (commit 9c53ffd, TaskContext 1483) only fires when cloudReadOk(token) is false, and it is already true for the whole session once the 12:00 load read succeeded. So the stale row goes through. storage.ts syncLoadByToken: `if (localDate > cloudDate)` keeps local only when strictly newer, so the tablet (lastDate yesterday) takes the cloud row (lastDate today) and runs save(cloud) over its newer local state. On main (13f14e6) nothing ran the day transition while the app was open. The only timer that wrote was Expedition.jsx's rangerArrived poll, which ran only while that screen was mounted. So an idle glance never wrote before this pass. The same-day case also breaks: a stale phone snapshot with an away trip that is due runs arriveTrip on resume and writes it. The tie rule then lets that stale cloud row beat the tablet's afternoon progress.
SAVES-1.fix: In useTripClock, record when the tab was hidden. On visibilitychange to visible, if dayKey(now) differs from state.lastDate, or the tab was hidden for more than about 5 minutes, call window.location.reload() instead of tick(). That way syncLoadByToken resolves against the cloud before any day transition or arrival runs. Keep the in-place checkNewDay/arriveTrip only for the 30 s interval while the tab stays visible, and skip the interval tick when document.visibilityState is not 'visible'. Add a test: a provider whose stale state has yesterday's lastDate resumes from hidden, and no profile_upsert fires before a reload.

SAVES-2.verified_evidence: The only savePendingHatch call is in OnboardingChain.jsx 107-117, inside NoProfileLanding's onBeforeOpen, and that only runs on the scan or code-field path (NoProfileLanding.jsx 104). The ?p= link path: AuthGate (App.jsx 708-710) calls getActiveToken(), which stores the URL token and strips it (profileToken.ts 73-88). No stash is written. TaskProvider then runs syncLoadByToken(token). On a fresh device getLocalProfileOwner() is null, so the local copy is kept as this card's. The hatched local state has kidIntroSeen and companionName but no onboardingDone or parentOnboardingDone (egg first, before the parent step), so localPristine is true. The website seed has parentOnboardingDone, so cloudFurther is true. The cloud wins and save(cloud) overwrites local. In OnboardingChain 68-77, takePendingHatch finds no stash and returns null, so the child is back at MeetRonki without the named dragon. Design 2.3 lists 'share link opened directly' as a supported path, and 2.4 promises that a local hatch is carried into a card that has not hatched yet. R7 kept that promise only for the scan path.
SAVES-2.fix: Keep storage.ts untouched (R7). Before the URL token is consumed, write the stash when it applies. The simplest place is AuthGate's mount effect, which runs before TaskProvider mounts because useAuth starts with loading=true. There: const urlTok = readTokenFromUrl(); if urlTok differs from the stored token, read the local mirror synchronously (JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('hdx2_drachennest'))). If it has kidIntroSeen and a companionName, has no onboardingDone, and getLocalProfileOwner() is null or equals urlTok, call savePendingHatch({ companionName, companionVariant, token: urlTok }). Only then call getActiveToken(). The existing takePendingHatch rules then apply unchanged. Add a test for the ?p= path.

SAVES-3.verified_evidence: TaskContext 1460-1505: the local save runs after 400 ms, the cloud save after 1500 ms, and both are cleared on every state change. departTrip (TaskContext 2300-2338) and receiveTreasure (2358-2370) do not change lastDate. So on a same-day cold start both copies carry today's date, and syncLoadByToken's strict `localDate > cloudDate` check hands the tie to the cloud. If the app is killed, or on iOS backgrounded (timers pause) and then evicted, before the 1.5 s cloud timer fires, the next cold start that day restores the pre-departure or pre-treasure cloud row over the newer local copy. The DepartureSheet or the treasure then replays. adventureCount is not doubled, because the restored row is from before the receive. The debounce and the tie rule already existed on main, so this pass does not add the mechanism. It does make it more likely, because the departure is now the last tap of the morning session. The result is a replayed moment, not lost progress, so COULD fits.
SAVES-3.fix: In TaskProvider, add a listener for visibilitychange to 'hidden' and for pagehide. It clears cloudTimer and, if there is an active token and storage.cloudReadOk(token) is true (keep the FC-01 guard), immediately calls storage.cloudSaveByToken(token, {...localRaw, ...stateRef.current}) as a best effort. Use a stateRef so the listener sees the latest state. storage.ts stays untouched.

LOOP-1.verified_evidence: returnBeat.js nestBeat, day block: `if (!firstDay && morning.total > 0 && morning.full && !tripToday)` returns 'departure'; otherwise 'stay'. The departure only happens when the child taps (RoomHub bye() -> departTrip('day') from DepartureCard or DepartureSheet); nothing departs on its own. isFirstDay stays true until adventureCount > 0. So on a morning install where the fire got full but nobody tapped before 11:00 (12:00 at weekends), the 30 s tick switches the mode to 'stay', the effect `if (mode !== 'departure') setDepartureOpen(false)` closes the sheet, and contextLineFor gives fd_start_day_01. On day 2+ the same state still departs. The guard cannot protect an afternoon install either: fireOfBlock gives bonus = floor(total/2), so full always needs at least ceil(total/2) real done morning tasks, and the Nest's day block only offers afternoonTasks (evening/hobby anchors). Downgraded to COULD: it needs day 1 plus no tap, and the child still gets the evening dream trip (lastTripDate is not today) and a treasure at breakfast.
LOOP-1.fix: In nestBeat's day branch, drop `!firstDay &&`, or keep a guard that is actually about the afternoon install: `(!firstDay || morning.lit - morning.bonus > 0)`. Add a returnBeat test: onboardingDate = today, adventureCount 0, enough morning slots done for full with the bonus, now 13:30 on a weekday, expect mode 'departure'.

LOOP-2.verified_evidence: TonightRitual.jsx: fireComplete() (completeTonight + departTrip('night') when hook.dream) runs only from the curtain timer (12000 ms after startCurtain) or a tap in the 'curtain' phase. The close button (`phase !== 'black'`, calls onClose) and ESC unmount the component, and the unmount cleanup clears curtainTimerRef, so nothing is committed. The hook line 'night_trip_01' plays when the 'hook' phase starts, about 6.5 s plus 12 s before the commit. Scenario confirmed: the hook is heard, the parent taps X during the lullaby, and there is no trip, no eveningRitualCompletedAt, and Ronki is home with nothing at breakfast. If the PWA is killed during the curtain, the same happens.
LOOP-2.fix: Commit when the promise is made: at the start of startCurtain (the hook was shown), or when handleTap enters 'hook' with hook.dream, call actions.completeTonight() and, if hook.dream, actions.departTrip('night'), guarded by completeFiredRef. LOOP-3.verified_evidence: RoomHub.jsx: the greeting effect (`greetDue && greetedRef.current !== today` -> sayPassing(greetId) + actions.markGreeted()) and the context-line effect (VoiceAudio.playLocalized(contextId) whenever contextId changes; spokenRef is reset to null in the `today` effect) do not check document.visibilityState or any user presence. RoomHub's own setInterval(30 s) and useTripClock's checkNewDay tick keep running while the Nest stays open. The day key is UTC (clock.ts dayKey), so it rolls over at 02:00 CEST / 01:00 CET. applyDayTransition rebuilds quests with done:false, and greetingFor gives a line because greetedDate is still yesterday. If the ritual was not done, the block is 'evening', the evening fire becomes 0 of n, the mode is 'fire', and at 02:00 the greeting plus task_ask_dinner play, and greetedDate is stamped. If the ritual was done, the block is 'night' until 04:00 (greetDue is false), then at 04:00 the morning greeting plus task_ask_wake play. Either way the child opening at 07:00 gets no return line, because greetedDate === today. It needs the Nest to stay mounted overnight (a screen left on, or a page that is still alive in the background), a case the code comments name on purpose ('the tablet sat on it overnight').
LOOP-3.fix: Gate automatic speech and markGreeted on presence: skip both when document.visibilityState !== 'visible', and do not speak for clock-only mode changes between the evening start and 06:00. Mark 'present' on pointerdown or on a visibilitychange to visible, then run the greeting and the context line; reset greetedRef and spokenRef on presence, not only on the day key. At minimum, call markGreeted only after a user interaction or a visible mount.

LOOP-4.verified_evidence: clock.ts dayKey = toISOString().slice(0,10) (UTC). TaskContext checkNewDay (polled every 30 s by useTripClock) compares prev.lastDate to dayKey(now), and applyDayTransition rebuilds quests. dayPhase keeps the evening block until 04:00 local. So at 01:00 CET / 02:00 CEST, during the evening block, the evening tasks done so far are wiped and the fire drops back. A dream trip after that point stamps lastTripDate with the new key, so the next morning's full fire gets tripToday true and no send-off. The impact is small: the dream trip still brings a treasure at 05:00, and it only affects children awake past 01:00/02:00.
LOOP-4.fix: For the loop's own keys (checkNewDay trigger, lastTripDate, greetedDate), use the local date of (now minus 4 h), which matches DAY_START, or at least let checkNewDay roll over only when blockAt(now) is not 'evening' or 'night'. Stamp a night trip's lastTripDate with the date of eveningStartFor(now).

LOOP-5.verified_evidence: checkNewDay: `if (prev.lastDate === dayKey(clockNow())) return prev; return applyDayTransition(prev);`, with the same inequality in the load path. A backwards key runs a full transition: quests are rebuilt with done:false, sm is recomputed, and lastGapDays = max(0, daysBetween(...)) = 0. Correcting the clock runs a second transition, with a gap measured from the wrong date. departTrip stamps lastTripDate from the wrong clock. arriveTrip only settles when now >= returnAt, so a trip sent while the clock was ahead stays away until that time. Rare (it needs a wrong device clock), and before this pass the load path already compared with !==, but the 30 s poll is new.
LOOP-5.fix: Transition only when dayKey(now) > prev.lastDate (ISO date strings compare correctly), in checkNewDay and in the load path. In arriveTrip and tripDue, treat a returnAt more than 24 h in the future as due.

LOOP-6.verified_evidence: ParentalDashboard RonkisTagSection: the Ferien switch calls patchState({ vacMode: v }) only (with the label 'Ab morgen kommen die Ferien-Aufgaben.'), so today's quests keep their s_* ids. A later same-day routine change calls setRoutine -> questsForRoutine(prev, r), which builds buildDay(!!prev.vacMode = true), giving ids v_wake, v_breakfast and so on (constants.ts), and looks them up in a map keyed by the old s_* ids. None match, so every main quest comes back done:false and the fire drops to 0 lit. Part of the claim is wrong: applyDayTransition only updates sm for the ids in s.quests (now v_*), so the s_* streaks are left as they were, not zeroed.
LOOP-6.fix: In questsForRoutine, fall back to matching by taskKind(id) (and anchor) when the id is missing, carrying done, completions and streak over. Or build with the vacMode that produced today's list (derived from the prefix of the current main quests) until the next day transition, which matches the switch's own 'ab morgen' promise.

LOOP-7.verified_evidence: Rehydration (TaskContext ~1365): `lastTripDate: typeof raw.lastTripDate === 'string' ? raw.lastTripDate : null`. On main there is no lastTripDate, so a save whose expedition left today on the old path (away/waiting, or already home with a log entry from today) loads with lastTripDate null. After the treasure is received, tonightHook sees lastTripDate !== today and a full evening fire, so hook.dream is true, and departTrip('night') passes its `prev.lastTripDate === key` guard: two trips on ship day. Only the ship night is affected, and the extra effect is a second treasure.
LOOP-7.fix: In rehydration, when lastTripDate is absent, backfill it from dayKey(expedition.departedAt) for an away or waiting trip, or else from the ts of the last expeditionLog entry, when that is today.

KIDUX-5.verified_evidence: On the last morning task, onTaskDone calls sayPassing('fire_lit_01', 2400) (RoomHub.jsx:284), which plays at 0 and sets passingUntil to about t+2400. In the same render the mode becomes 'departure', and the context effect (244-249) schedules fire_full_morning_01 at max(400, passingUntil - now), about 2.4 s. ffprobe gives de_fire_full_morning_01.mp3 a length of 3.90 s, so it runs to about 6.3 s. The departure effect (263-267) opens the sheet at DEPARTURE_DELAY_MS = 3800 ms. StepStones (speakOnMount, StepStones.jsx:35-36) then calls playLocalized(grow line, 300) at about 4.1 s, and VoiceAudio.play calls this.stop() (voiceAudio.ts play/doPlay). The line is cut after about 1.7 s ('Mein Feuer ist ganz warm!' survives, 'Jetzt kann ich losfliegen.' does not), every departure. The fixed sheet also covers the bubble text.
KIDUX-5.fix: Open the sheet after the context line ends: set the delay to about 2400 + 3900 + 400 ms (roughly 6.7 s), or schedule it from the audio 'ended' event (a VoiceAudio play-with-callback for Ronki lines). A cheaper fix is to raise StepStones' speakOnMount delay while departure is open so it starts after the line.

KIDUX-6.verified_evidence: The dashboard Ferien switch (ParentalDashboard.jsx:642-647, line 'Ab morgen kommen die Ferien-Aufgaben.') calls patchState({ vacMode: v }) and leaves today's quests alone, so they stay s_*. setRoutine (TaskContext.tsx:2372-2382) calls questsForRoutine (873-880), which runs buildDay(!!prev.vacMode, routine). With vacMode now true, buildDay uses VACATION_QUESTS (helpers.ts:34), whose ids are v_* (constants.ts:81-94). old.get(q.id) misses every one, so every main quest comes back fresh with done false and the done s_* quests are dropped. A parent who turns Ferien on and then changes the routine in the same session resets today's fire to cold. Turning Ferien off during the holidays does the same the other way round.
KIDUX-6.fix: In questsForRoutine, pick the source list from today's main quests (v_ prefix present means vacation), not from prev.vacMode. Or match old quests by taskKind across prefixes and carry over done, completions and streak. vacMode then only takes effect at the next day transition, which is what the switch label promises.

KIDUX-7.verified_evidence: returnBeat.js:98-107: in the day block, departure needs !firstDay. isFirstDay (fire.ts:48-50) is true all install day while adventureCount is 0. KIDUX-7.fix: Apply the day-1 no-send-off only when onboarding finished in the day block (store the install block, or the onboarding time, and compare it with the morning end). Otherwise let a morning fire that is full keep the departure.
